pr_body:
##### Summary
Fixes #8497 

This PR changes configurations on master Netdata to support newest TLS versions.
##### Component Name
Web
Stream
##### Test Plan
The test plan is majority focus in the stream communication, because we are assuming that the tester will use the browser to access the `master` to see information related to his slaves.

The following tests were done with this PR:

###### First test 
This test is the basis for the next tests considering that we will only change few values after this.

1 - Create key and certificate using openssl ( openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -days 365 -nodes -x509 -sha512 -subj "/C=US/ST=Denied/L=Somewhere/O=Dis/CN=www.example.com" -keyout key.pem  -out cert.pem ). It is possible to use self signed certificate.
2 - Set at least following variables inside `netdata.conf` on your master:
```
[web]
	ssl key = /etc/netdata/ssl/key.pem
	ssl certificate = /etc/netdata/ssl/cert.pem
```
3 - Start your master
4 - Set the following variables inside your `stream.conf` on your slave:
```
[stream]
    destination = 192.168.0.12:19999:SSL
    ssl skip certificate verification = yes
```
4 - Start your slave

With the previous options Netdata will start streaming using TLS 1.3 case your system supports it, to confirm, please, run the next command and verify its output:

```
openssl s_client -connect localhost:19999
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.3
    Cipher    : TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
   .....
```

I am omitting parts of the message, because they are not necessary to confirm the protocol used.
##### Second Test
Now we only need to change configuration on `master` side, please, remember to stop your `slave` before you stop your master and only start your `slave` after to start your `master`.

The second test will rename options and bring a new option to set tls version: 

```
[web]
	tls key = /etc/netdata/ssl/key.pem
	tls certificate = /etc/netdata/ssl/cert.pem
        tls version = 1.3
```
1 - Stop Slave
2 - Stop master
3 - Start master
4 - Start slave

##### Third test

This test will change the `tls version` on master side only, on slave this is set during the handshake process.

```
[web]
   tls version = 1.2
```

1 - Stop Slave
2 - Stop master
3 - Start master
4 - Start slave

To confirm that we have `TLS 1.2`, please, run:

```
openssl s_client -connect localhost:19999
SSL-Session:
    Protocol  : TLSv1.2
    Cipher    : ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384

```

##### Fourth test
On this final test we will set the `tls version` and `tls ciphers`:

```
[web]
   tls version = 1.3
   tls ciphers = TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256:TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```

1 - Stop Slave
2 - Stop master
3 - Start master
4 - Start slave
##### Additional Information
